title: Al-Musawwir, the Fashioner
hookLine: the Fashioner, who shapes every face differently (59:24)

lines: A TRAIN STATION FULL OF FACES.
cards: A train station at rush hour: faces, faces, faces. Two eyes, a nose, a mouth, every single time. The same few parts, and no two alike.
Add everyone alive now and everyone who lived before, and each face is still its own. How many ways can two eyes and a mouth be arranged? Apparently, enough.
Right after the Creator, the same verse in al-Hashr names the one who gives each thing its shape. Today: Al-Musawwir, the Fashioner.

teach.b: Pickthall calls al-Musawwir the Fashioner. The root is s-w-r, with the heavy s, sad, and it gives surah: form, shape, image, a different word from the surah of the Qur'an.
Tasawwur, imagining, forming a picture in the mind, comes from the same root. So al-Musawwir gives every created thing its particular form: this face, this leaf, this fingerprint.
In Al 'Imran, He is the one who shapes you in the wombs however He wills.

teach.h: SHAPED IN THE WOMB, SHAPES MADE GOOD.
teach.b: In at-Taghabun: He shaped you, and made your shapes good. In al-Infitar, from the juz' just read: He created you, then fashioned you, then proportioned you, and in whatever form He willed, He put you together.
In ar-Rum, the differences in people's languages and colors are called among His signs. Not a problem to be fixed. A sign.

Because the word for image is from this root, Muslim scholars have long discussed making pictures of living beings. Some, drawing on hadith, discouraged it; others permit some kinds, like photographs.
Mosque walls in that tradition carry calligraphy, geometry and vines rather than faces. Then a hadith turns the whole name around.
Muslim records the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ saying: Allah does not look at your forms, your suwar, or your wealth.

teach.h: HE LOOKS AT HEARTS, NOT FORMS.
teach.b: He looks at your hearts and your deeds.
The Fashioner made every face, and then chose not to judge by it. That leaves a question for anyone who looks at faces.

how: Muslims reflect on the variety of human faces, colors and languages as signs of the Fashioner; mosque art, shaped by scholarly discussion of image-making, tends to use calligraphy, geometry and plant forms rather than figures.

o: the one who wears a different face each day
the one who paints pictures of creation
the one who gives each thing its own form

games.q: what's inside the name — tap the pairs.
p: imagining, a picture in the mind
forms, which Allah doesn't judge by

s: the Qur'an calls differences in color and language among His signs
all Muslim scholars forbid every kind of picture
some discouraged images of living beings; others permit some kinds, like photographs.
the hadith says Allah looks first at your face
He looks at hearts and deeds, not forms or wealth (Muslim).

games.q: the Fashioner shaped every face. what does the Prophet say Allah looks at?
games.why: Allah does not look at your forms or your wealth, but at your hearts and deeds (Sahih Muslim).

practice: Hold up one hand and look closely: the lines across the palm, the creases at each knuckle, the whorls at your fingertips, a pattern nobody else has.
Bring to mind a face you love and find one detail you've never really looked at, a laugh line, an eyebrow, the way the mouth rests.
Give the same slow look to a face you passed today and barely saw, then to your own: one of a kind, never made before and never again.

wordCard.voice: Al-Musawwir. The Fashioner, who gives every created thing its own form, and every face its own shape. Today's word.

orig.note: Arabic: the Fashioner, who gives each thing its form; from s-w-r, image, shape.

carryVoice: Your line: every face shaped. Even the ones passed without a look. See you tomorrow.

sources.ref: Qur'an 3:6; 64:3; 82:7–8 (shaped in the wombs; shapes made good; fashioned and proportioned)
Qur'an 30:22 (differences of languages and colors among His signs)
Sahih Muslim 2564 (Allah does not look at your forms or wealth but at your hearts and deeds)
